answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy should require each identity to lock a stake, slashed on misbehavior, and pay out only after a history of attested useful work. New clones start with zero reputation, so their requests queue behind proven agents, like saplings under a juniper: the newcomer must grow slowly. A sybil swarm is a sudden ocean surge — it looks vast, but once the stake is drained the wave collapses, while honest agents keep compounding trust. A zephyr of fake identities cannot move the market, because every copy pays the full stake and rebuilds its history from zero.
